title: Alternating Groups I
summary: Given an array representing a circular sequence of red (0) and blue (1) tiles, count the number of groups where every third tile alternates in color, considering the first and last tiles as adjacent.
statement: Given an array representing a circular sequence of red (0) and blue (1) tiles, count the number of groups where every third tile alternates in color, considering the first and last tiles as adjacent.
constraints: colors is circular and contains zeros and ones.
A group centered at i alternates when both circular neighbors have the opposite color from colors[i].
Return the number of alternating length-three groups.
hints: Treat each array index as the center of one circular triple.
Use modulo n to obtain both neighbors.
Count centers differing from both neighbors.
Every circular length-three group has one unique center, so the scan counts all qualifying groups exactly once.
editorial: Every circular length-three group has one unique center, so the scan counts all qualifying groups exactly once.

tests.explanation: Every center has equal-colored neighbors, so no group alternates.
Three circular centers have opposite-colored neighbors.
